stories.title: Trade and tariffs
stories.detail: Above its own baseline: 3 headlines against a normal of 0.8, and new language today (sanction, warns). That is a change, not just continuing coverage.
stories.why: Indirect but real. Tariffs are an inflation impulse and a growth drag at once, which is the hardest combination for the Fed and therefore raises uncertainty about the rate path.
stories.counterweight: Also dollar-positive in the short run, which works against gold. The net effect is genuinely ambiguous and often small.
stories.duration: Weeks, when it changes the inflation outlook. Announcement headlines alone rarely stick.
stories.spoken_why: Tariffs raise prices and slow growth at the same time, which is the hardest combination for the Federal Reserve to answer.
stories.read: Broadly consistent, though Nasdaq 100, Gold, WTI crude and 1 others are not playing along. One asset out of line is usually its own story; several is a reason to doubt the read.

stories.title: Wider Middle East
stories.detail: 11 headlines, which is about its normal of 12.2 after 30 days running. Continuing coverage rather than escalation - gold has priced this.
stories.why: Haven demand, mostly. Moves gold hard on the first day of a genuine escalation and then fades, because the region's conflicts rarely touch US rate expectations directly.
stories.counterweight: Heavily discounted by markets through repetition - a headline that would have moved gold $40 in the first month of a conflict moves it $5 in the ninth.
stories.duration: Hours to days. The shortest-lived of the major flashpoints unless it pulls Iran in directly.
stories.spoken_why: It moves gold on haven demand, but the effect fades fast because these headlines rarely touch US interest rates.
stories.read: Mostly not following - Gold, Nasdaq 100, US 10-year yield and 2 others are all going the other way. Either this is already in the price, or something bigger is driving the tape today.

stories.title: US / Israel – Iran
stories.detail: Coverage is below its own normal and carrying de-escalation language. Any risk premium here should be fading.
stories.why: The one flashpoint that hits gold through every channel at once. Safe-haven bid on the headline, Treasuries bid so nominal and real yields fall, and - uniquely - a credible threat to the Strait of Hormuz spikes crude, which lifts inflation expectations. Roughly a fifth of seaborne oil passes through that strait.
stories.counterweight: The dollar is also a haven, so risk-off bids the dollar too and cancels part of gold's gain. This is why some escalation days produce a far smaller gold move than the headlines imply.
stories.duration: Days. Gold spikes on the exchange of fire and gives most of it back within a week unless the oil disruption is real and sustained, because only then does it reach the Fed's reaction function.

stories.spoken_why: It reaches gold through three channels at once: the haven bid, lower real yields, and the risk to oil coming through the Strait of Hormuz.
stories.read: Broadly consistent, though WTI crude, VIX are not playing along. One asset out of line is usually its own story; several is a reason to doubt the read.

profile.name: FOMC Rate Decision
profile.what: The Federal Open Market Committee sets the target range for the federal funds rate. Announced at 19:00 UK (14:00 ET), followed 30 minutes later by the Chair's press conference.
profile.who: Federal Reserve, eight scheduled meetings a year
profile.why_gold: Gold pays no interest, so its opportunity cost is the real yield on cash and Treasuries. Anything that lowers expected real rates raises gold, and vice versa. This is the single most direct transmission channel there is.
profile.watch: The decision itself is usually priced in. The move comes from three other things: changes to the statement's language, the dot plot on projection meetings, and the tone of the press conference - which frequently reverses the initial statement reaction.
profile.gotchas: Two-leg event. Gold often moves one way on the 19:00 statement and the opposite way during the 19:30 presser. Judging the day on the first ten minutes is how people get caught.
profile.prior_move_usd: 20-60 on the day, more on projection meetings

profile.who: Federal Reserve, eight scheduled meetings a year
profile.why_gold: Gold pays no interest, so its opportunity cost is the real yield on cash and Treasuries. Anything that lowers expected real rates raises gold, and vice versa. This is the single most direct transmission channel there is.
profile.watch: The decision itself is usually priced in. The move comes from three other things: changes to the statement's language, the dot plot on projection meetings, and the tone of the press conference - which frequently reverses the initial statement reaction.
profile.gotchas: Two-leg event. Gold often moves one way on the 19:00 statement and the opposite way during the 19:30 presser. Judging the day on the first ten minutes is how people get caught.
profile.prior_move_usd: 20-60 on the day, more on projection meetings
